meta.title: Yukino Sentry — Frontend observability, five lines away
meta.description: Yukino Sentry is a framework-agnostic browser monitoring SDK for errors, HTTP, Web Vitals, page views, declarative clicks, exposure tracking, white-screen detection, offline reporting and screen recordings.

hero.badge: Plugins, offline reporting & dev-time source maps
hero.description: Yukino Sentry is a framework-agnostic monitoring SDK that catches errors, HTTP, Web Vitals, page views, clicks, exposure, blank screens and sessions — from five lines of code.

features.title: One SDK,
features.description: Everything the browser can tell you about a session — errors, network, performance, behaviour and reliability — captured by a single, fully typed client that never blocks your app.

errorCapture.title: Error capture
errorCapture.description: Runtime errors, console.error, resource load failures and unhandled rejections are classified, deduplicated and batched automatically.

httpCapture.title: HTTP capture
httpCapture.description: XHR and fetch are instrumented with status classification, server-timing parsing and 8 KB body capture on failures only.

webVitals.title: Web Vitals
webVitals.description: LCP, FCP, CLS, INP and TTFB alongside a custom First Screen Paint metric measured from real DOM mutations.

navigationTiming.title: Navigation timing
navigationTiming.description: DNS, TLS, TTFB, DOM processing, resource load and redirect breakdowns from the Navigation Timing API.

pageViews.title: Page views & dwell
pageViews.description: Automatic PageLoad, route-change PVs and dwell time flushed on pagehide so mobile sessions are never lost.

declarativeClicks.title: Declarative clicks
declarativeClicks.description: Zero-code click tracking through yukino-sentry-* attributes with params, element path and viewport coordinates.

exposure.title: Exposure tracking
exposure.description: Measure how long any element stays visible with IntersectionObserver thresholds and custom params per target.

whiteScreen.title: White-screen detection
whiteScreen.description: 18-point viewport sampling plus a skeleton-screen baseline mode catches blank pages before users report them.

screenRecording.title: Screen recording
screenRecording.description: A gzipped rrweb rolling window is attached to the errors and requests you care about, decodable with one helper.

offlineReporting.title: Offline reporting
offlineReporting.description: Events queue in localStorage, ship with sendBeacon and recover with an exponential backoff health probe.

breadcrumbs.title: Breadcrumbs
breadcrumbs.description: A bounded trail of HTTP, click, route, resource and code events attached to every error-class report.

visitorIdentity.title: Visitor identity
visitorIdentity.description: Anonymous visitor ids, persistent device ids and per-tab session ids resolve users across refreshes.

reporterHooks.title: Reporter hooks
reporterHooks.description: beforeSend, beforeSendBatch and afterSend let you redact, filter or enrich every event before it leaves the browser.

pluginSystem.title: Plugin system
pluginSystem.description: Extend the core with any SentryPlugin implementation — everything is tree-shakeable and framework free.

reactVue.title: React & Vue
reactVue.description: A React ErrorBoundary and a Vue 3 plugin are published as dedicated subpath exports so nothing extra is bundled.

devSourceMaps.title: Dev-time source maps
devSourceMaps.description: Vite and webpack dev-server plugins resolve reported stacks back to original source with inline snippets.

developer.title: Built for the people
developer.description: No agents to install, no dashboards to learn. A tiny client, honest defaults and escape hatches everywhere.
developer.terminalOutput2: ready to monitor — no agent, no build step
developer.card1Description: Drop in the SDK and you are done. The core is tree-shakeable, framework agnostic and safe to import on any page.
developer.card2Description: Code, resource, runtime and unknown errors each take a dedicated path, so routing, dedup and batching behave predictably.
developer.card3Title: See the session, not just the stack
developer.card3Description: Breadcrumbs and a compressed rrweb window replay the moments before a failure — clicks, routes, requests and the DOM.
developer.card4Title: Stay in the flow, even offline
developer.card4Description: Events persist to localStorage, ship with sendBeacon and recover through an exponential health probe when the network returns.

analytics.title: Understand journeys,
analytics.description: Behavioural signals live next to your error data. See which page a session lingered on, what people clicked and how long a promotion stayed on screen.
analytics.dwellNote: Dwell under 100 ms is dropped as noise. The final window is flushed on pagehide so mobile sessions are never lost.
analytics.exposureNote: One observer per unique threshold, reused across every target. Reported when an element leaves the viewport after being visible.
analytics.attr4Description: Any other attribute becomes a param.
analytics.card1Description: PageLoad, HistoryChange and HashChange are captured from day one, each with its URL, referrer and entry time.
analytics.card2Description: Clicks report coordinates, element path, custom params and resolved event id — plain clicks stay out of your bill.

performance.title: Real user metrics,
performance.description: Web Vitals and a full navigation timing breakdown run beside your errors, so a slow request and a crash are one story.
performance.source1Description: paint, DOM, load, DNS, TCP, TLS, TTFB, transfer and redirect breakdown.
performance.source2Description: Snapshot of every buffered resource with cache and transfer sizes.
performance.source3Description: Per-resource durations as they complete, with element fallback.
performance.source4Description: Main-thread tasks that block interaction, reported as entries.
performance.source5Description: Chrome-only memory attribution when the API is available.
performance.ownDescription: Any timing you own can be sent as a performance event with tracePerformance.

reliability.title: Reporting that survives
reliability.description: A production monitoring client cannot afford to lose data or block the page. Yukino Sentry keeps a durable queue, ships asynchronously and never lets one failed batch stall the rest.
reliability.guarantee1Description: Breadcrumbs and the error-dedup set are LRU-capped, so long-lived SPAs never grow without limit.
reliability.guarantee2Description: ignoreErrors matches message substrings or patterns; excludeAPIs uses exact URLs or regex.
reliability.guarantee3Description: A failed batch is pushed back to the queue head and persisted, so ordering is preserved end-to-end.

plugins.title: Optional power,
plugins.description: Capabilities like performance, screen recording and exposure tracking live in @yukino.js/sentry/plugins. Import only what you enable — the core entry stays lean.
plugins.plugin1Tagline: Field performance, out of the box.
plugins.plugin1Bullet1: LCP, FCP, CLS, INP and TTFB from web-vitals
plugins.plugin1Bullet2: Custom First Screen Paint from DOM mutations
plugins.plugin1Bullet3: Navigation, resource, long-task and memory data
plugins.plugin1Bullet4: Zero constructor options, safe capability checks
plugins.plugin2Bullet1: Rolling rrweb window, gzip + base64 encoded
plugins.plugin2Bullet3: Canvas recording and inline images enabled
plugins.plugin3Bullet2: Visible duration, show times and custom params
plugins.extendDescription: Implement SentryPlugin and get lifecycle-aware init() and optional destroy() hooks. Plugins are registered once, stored in a set and cleaned up with destroy().

frameworks.title: First-class where it counts.
frameworks.description: React and Vue ship as dedicated subpath exports. Everyone else uses the same typed core with reportFrameworkError.
frameworks.noteVanilla: The core entry is framework agnostic and safe to import anywhere. No framework dependency is ever pulled into your bundle.
frameworks.noteReact: The boundary reports caught render errors as React events with the component stack. Async callbacks, event handlers and SSR errors still need traceError().
frameworks.noteVue: vuePlugin wraps app.config.errorHandler, reports Vue errors with the instance and info string, then calls any handler you had installed before.
frameworks.highlight1Body: Caught React errors carry the ErrorInfo component stack straight into the report context.
frameworks.highlight2Body: The Vue plugin captures the previous handler and always delegates after reporting.
frameworks.highlight3Body: Call reportFrameworkError with EventType.OtherFrameworks and your own context object.
frameworks.warning: Boundaries only catch synchronous render errors. Use traceError() for async and event-handler failures.

quickstart.title: From zero to production
quickstart.description: No agent, no config file, no build plugin required. This is the entire happy path.
quickstart.step1Description: One package. React, Vue, Vite and webpack are optional peers you only install when you use them.
quickstart.step2Description: Point the SDK at your report endpoint. Everything else falls back to sensible defaults.
quickstart.step3Description: Performance, screen recording and exposure tracking are opt-in and tree-shakeable.
quickstart.step4Description: Send business events, timings and manual errors with the same pipeline and hooks.
quickstart.guardDescription: The SDK is safe to guard with isInitialized(), can be fully torn down with destroy(), and keeps globalThis.__sentry__ available for live inspection while debugging.

options.title: Every knob,
options.description: init() accepts a partial options object. Anything you omit falls back to a default, and zod validates the merged result before a single listener is installed.
options.group1Blurb: Everything you need to get a project reporting.
options.group2Blurb: Turn individual capture layers on or off at init time.
options.group3Blurb: Sampling, batching, retry and detection behaviour.
options.group4Blurb: Transform reports and control where the offline queue lives.
options.eventTypesDescription: Every report carries a typed EventType so you can route, sample or drop signals downstream without guessing.

rows.dsn: Report endpoint. Must be non-empty for init to succeed.
rows.projectId: Frontend project identifier attached to every event.
rows.userId: Current user identifier, updatable with setUserId().
rows.disabled: Apply options but skip all listeners and reporting.
rows.debug: Stream styled SDK activity to the console at runtime.
rows.enableError: Runtime, console.error and resource error capture.
rows.enableWhiteScreen: Sample the viewport for blank pages after load.
rows.enableFingerprint: Resolve an anonymous visitor id with FingerprintJS.
rows.enableHttpPerformance: Report successful requests as performance events.
rows.repeatCodeError: Report duplicate code errors instead of deduplicating.
rows.tracesSampleRate: Sampling rate between 0 and 1 applied to every payload.
rows.maxBreadcrumbs: FIFO capacity of the breadcrumb buffer.
rows.cacheMaxLength: Maximum batch size before an immediate flush.
rows.maxQueueLength: Maximum queued events while offline or retrying.
rows.retryIntervalMilliseconds: Cap for the exponential server-recovery probe.
rows.screenRecordDurationMs: Rolling rrweb window length in milliseconds.
rows.clickThrottleDelay: Throttle window for click capture; 0 disables it.
rows.hasSkeleton: Compare samples against a skeleton baseline.
rows.rootCssSelectors: Selectors treated as empty during white-screen detection.
rows.ignoreErrors: Message substrings or patterns that skip reporting.
rows.excludeAPIs: Exact URLs or patterns excluded from HTTP capture.
rows.beforeSend: Transform or drop a single event before queueing.
rows.beforeSendBatch: Filter or rewrite a batch before transport.
rows.afterSend: Observe batches after a successful transport.
rows.beforeBreadcrumb: Synchronously transform a breadcrumb before it is stored.
rows.offlineCacheKey: localStorage key used for the offline queue.

events.vue: Vue error handled by the app.

api.title: A small surface,
api.description: Everything you can call lives on the root entry. No hidden singletons, no framework coupling — just functions with obvious contracts.

items.init: Validates options with zod, writes runtime config and installs every enabled capture layer.
items.destroy: Restores decorated globals, tears down plugins and resets all session state.
items.isInitialized: Returns true once setup has completed and false after destroy.
items.enablePlugin: Initializes and registers any number of plugin instances.
items.traceError: Routes an error through the full classification pipeline manually.
items.tracePerformance: Report a custom performance metric as an OK event.
items.traceCustomEvent: Emit an arbitrary business event with optional context.
items.tracePageView: Manually record a page view, useful for virtual routes.
items.reportFrameworkError: Report React, Vue or any other framework error with explicit context.
items.setUserId: Attach the current user id to subsequent reports.
items.setVisitorId: Bind a backend-known visitor id to the session.
items.flushOfflineCache: Load the persisted queue and attempt to send it now.
items.hooks: Register reporter hooks programmatically after init.
items.getIdentity: Read anonymousId, visitorId, userId and their presence flags.

integrations.title: Readable stacks
integrations.description: Both dev-server plugins mock your report endpoint so nothing hits production, then map bundled positions back to the original source with inline snippets.
integrations.tool1Blurb: Intercepts the mock endpoint, writes timestamped JSONL logs and resolves stacks from the in-memory module graph.
integrations.tool2Blurb: Collects emitted .map assets with assetEmitted and enriches error records before writing them to disk.
integrations.sourcemapDescription: Error, stack-like and framework records are enriched with original file, line, column, symbol name and a three-line snippet on each side of the failing line. Resolution failures stay silent and never corrupt the raw report.

cta.title: Start catching what breaks
cta.description: Install the SDK, point it at an endpoint and ship. Yukino Sentry handles the classification, batching, retries and session context for you.

footer.description: A framework-agnostic browser monitoring SDK for errors, network, performance, behaviour and reliability. Built to be small, typed and pleasant to integrate.
